title: The cameras
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting, empty mid-century office tower at night, flickering fluorescent green-white light, long polished corridors and brass elevator doors, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 2. Camera 13 shows an office full of people. At 1 AM. 📹

Original fiction. Part 3 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: Last time: at 1:13 AM, the Harrow Tower's elevator rode up to a thirteenth floor. The building only has twelve.
scenes.image: an empty elevator car glowing in a dark lobby, its doors wide open

scenes.narration: Tess didn't ride it. She went back to her desk and did what guards do. She checked the cameras.
scenes.image: a woman security guard leaning toward a wall of monitors at night, her face lit grey-blue

scenes.narration: The system lists every camera in the building. Lobby. Garage. Stairwells. Every floor. She'd scrolled past it a hundred times.
scenes.image: a guard's hand on a computer mouse in a dark security office, monitors glowing above

scenes.narration: Tonight there was one more. Camera thirteen. Online.
scenes.image: a single monitor brightening in a dark security office, its picture still hazy

scenes.narration: She clicked it. The picture came up grainy and yellow. An office. Old wooden desks. Heavy typewriters. Ashtrays. Wood paneling.
scenes.image: grainy surveillance still of a 1950s office with wooden desks, typewriters and green desk lamps

scenes.narration: And it was full. Thirty people at work. Men in shirtsleeves. Women in cardigans. Phones she couldn't hear. At one thirty in the morning.
scenes.image: grainy image of 1950s office workers bent over desks under fluorescent light, cigarette smoke hanging in the air

scenes.narration: Nobody looked up. Nobody stopped. They just worked, and worked, like the shift would never end.
scenes.image: close-up of a 1950s office worker's hands typing endlessly at an old typewriter, grainy and yellowed

scenes.narration: Tess called the day guard at home. He answered on the first ring. Like he'd been sitting by the phone.
scenes.image: an older man sitting in a dark kitchen holding an old phone to his ear, eyes open wide

scenes.narration: Are they working? he asked. She said yes. He let out a long breath. Good. Worry when they stop.
scenes.image: a woman guard pressing a phone to her ear at a security desk, her eyes on a glowing monitor

scenes.narration: She looked back at the screen. Every typewriter had stopped. And every face on camera thirteen had turned, slowly, toward the lens.
scenes.image: grainy surveillance image of a 1950s office where every worker has turned to stare directly at the camera
